cohort: The study included 312 pregnant women presenting for their first antenatal visit before 24 weeks of gestation at Kanachur Institute of Medical Sciences, Mangalore.
finding: Early maternal hyperglycemia, diagnosed before 24 weeks of gestation, was significantly associated with increased risks of adverse feto-maternal outcomes, including pre-eclampsia, preterm birth, macrosomia, and NICU admission.
mod_finding: The hyperglycemia group showed a significantly higher incidence of primary cesarean delivery (35.4% vs. 19.3%) compared to the normoglycemic group.
birth_weight: Macrosomia (18.8% vs. 6.8%) was a measured outcome, indicating a focus on larger birth weights.
gest_age: Participants were enrolled before 24 weeks of gestation, and preterm birth (12.5% vs. 4.9%) was an outcome.
